messages:
arya: Spoke with infra about cross-region fallback semantics. Need clear contract for request affinity when routing across hosted/dedicated/private.

Tomas: problem: stateful requests (streaming chat with client-side seq ids) get dropped when we bounce between environments because runtime affinity lost. Proposed: add sticky-affinity token returned on initial connection and accepted across hosting modes.

arya: sticky token should be short-lived and tied to a request id. It must not confer long-term auth. Suggest: X-Affinity-Token: base64(<rand>-<epoch>) with TTL enforced by controlplane and runtime.

infra-bot: note: performance impact: affinity lookups add ~0.5ms p95. acceptable?

Tomas: yes but we can cache affinity locally in runtime for TTL to avoid controlplane hop for every request. Only check controlplane on miss.

arya: edge cases: when runtime evicts cache and new runtime doesn't yet have state, fallback logic must include rehydration: if hosted has cached KV, it can attempt state sync from controlplane-backed snapshot store.

ops-bot: runbook reference: https://redwood-internal/rr/runbooks/affinity-failure-rehydrate

Tomas: security note: affinity token must be opaque in logs. Don't surface in SLO dashboards.

arya: rollout: implement token header + local cache + backup snapshot store reads for 403/404 affinity misses. Canary on dedicated pools with streaming apps.

Tomas: owners: runtime (me) for token logic, infra (arya) for cache config + snapshot store interface.

infra-bot: alert: 6189003336 - 5% client stream reconnects in dedicated-asia-1 after affinity_cache_tuning.

arya: i'll tune cache sizes and TTL. Tomas: let's add metrics: affinity.miss_rate and affinity.rehydrate_lat_ms.

Tomas: will add headers: X-Affinity-Token, X-Affinity-Rehydrated.
